text:
Alyssa: quick WIP dashboard pushed — comparing hitmap vs token-saved across models/routes/customers. saw a surprising drop in prompt-hit % for small-context routes after last kernel selection tweak.

Raj: link?

Alyssa: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/prefetch-vs-token-savings (WIP) — panels: per-model hit-rate, per-route token-saved waterfall, per-customer heatstrip.

Simon: saw that too. short sequences (<=64 tokens) switched kernels more aggressively after v2.1.4, which increased decoding overhead and seems to reduce effective prefix reuse.

Maria: profiling snapshot attached: p50 unchanged, p95 +18ms, p99 +60ms on mantic-7b-small for route /search/summarize. shows extra memcpy in attention kernel.

Derek: FYI we also adjusted KV cache eviction TTL last week (reduced from 15m -> 5m) for memory pressure on dedicated pools. could explain warmup churn for low-volume customers.

Alyssa: good call. dashboard shows tenant slice "acme-inc" hit-rate fell from 48% -> 23% same window as TTL change. token-saved delta ~ -12k tokens/hour.

ops-bot: alert: cache-hit-drop anomaly for model=mantic-7b-small on 2026-03-11 14:02 UTC — severity: medium.

Raj: can you paste the query you used for token-saved? want to reproduce.

Alyssa: sure — SQL used to generate waterfall is below:
```sql
SELECT tenant_id, route, model, sum(tokens_saved) as tokens_saved, avg(hit_rate) as hit_rate
FROM prefetch_metrics
WHERE ts BETWEEN now() - interval '2h' AND now()
GROUP BY tenant_id, route, model
ORDER BY tokens_saved desc
LIMIT 200;
```

Maria: ran microbench on v2.1.3 vs v2.1.4 — kernel selection path increased branch mispredicts for short sequences. attaching flame: more time in kernel_dispatch() and memcpy.

Simon: that suggests kernel heuristic picks a kernel optimized for long seqs even when kv-cache length is small. we should add a fallback: if prefix_hit > X and seq_len <= Y prefer small-seq kernel.

Derek: also confirm that eviction change caused more cold starts for low QPS tenants. their warmup success depends on prefetch policy (we were using topk=10). maybe raise topk to 20 for low-volume tenants or increase TTL back to 10m.

Raj: propose immediate mitigations: 1) revert kernel selection tweak on canary, 2) set TTL to 10m for affected dedicated pools, 3) add dashboard annotations for deploys/ttl changes so we correlate faster.

Alyssa: agreed. I'll add canary revert and post PR. created a dashboard annotation event for the kernel deploy and TTL change (links in panel).

Maria: I'll run a focused prefix-warmup sim: synthesize requests for acme-inc and measure hit ramp across topk settings. will post results in this thread.

Simon: I'll add a small experiment in kernel selector: prefer small-kernel for seq<=64 when prefix_hit_estimate > 0.2. low-risk toggle.

Derek: tagging ops: @ops-team — can you hold TTL change rollback until Maria gives sim results? if sim shows benefits, ops can revert quickly.

Alyssa: thanks — action items: (1) Alyssa — canary revert & annotation, (2) Maria — warmup sim for topk/TTL, (3) Simon — selector toggle experiment, (4) Derek — prepare TTL rollback plan. update this thread with commit/PR links. :thumbsup:

Raj: nice. also let's add a per-customer token-saved anomaly alert (delta over 1h > 5k tokens) so we catch regressions earlier.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-118 — cache-hit drop investigation mailbox: infra-alerts@redwood.ai

Alyssa: posting quick checklist for dashboard owners — add these panels: model-hit-trend (7d), per-route-token-saved, per-tenant-hit-decomp, deploy-annotation-stream, kernel-timeline. keep thresholds conservative.

Maria: sim initial: topk=10 -> hit ramp to 22% in 30m, topk=20 -> ramp to 41% in 30m. will attach CSV.

Derek: that delta matches the token-saved numbers Alyssa saw. ops ready to roll TTL to 10m on dedicated pools if we greenlight.

Simon: I'll ship selector toggle behind feature flag and run canary with model=mantic-7b-small.

Alyssa: thanks team — once PRs linked I'll mark the dashboard annotation with the PR id and close the loop.

Raj: appreciate the quick triage. we should also record the kernel heuristic regression in the perf-regressions doc with links to this thread.

Alyssa: noted. will add to perf-regressions tracker.
